newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's biggest union body calls two-day strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's biggest union body calls two-day strike.

text.p: South Korea's biggest union body on Thursday called for a two-day strike of all its members starting next Tuesday.

The President of the Federation of Korean Trade Unions, which claims 1.2 million members, urged electricity, port and railway workers to go on partial strike and all other unionists to join a full stoppage.
"The federation calls on all its members to join the largest strike ever, led especially by the public sector," Park In-sang told a news conference.

City buses around the nation would be halted along with subway lines in Seoul under the federation's control. Park said no decision had been made on whether to join forces with the smaller Korean Confederation of Trade Unions in industrial action aimed at forcing the government to dump a new labour law that allows companies to lay off workers.

He also demanded the government halt legal action against union leaders and strikers. On Thursday state prosecutors said they would seek arrest warrants for seven confederation leaders, including president Kwon Young-kil.
